mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 4% triggers a recessionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months, coupled with rising real savings (RSAFS), indicates supply-side stress and reduced corporate capacity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 98 for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS rising for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which correlates with higher consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 AND UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 99 for six consecutive months, regardless of monetary policy stance, indicates deepening supply chain disruptions, which depress earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 95% confidence.
